record.prompt: Our API gateway runs 4 worker processes (deploy/server.conf) and limits each API key to 100 requests a minute in gateway/limits.py. Read https://docs.quillon.example/config and tell me whether a key really gets 100 per minute overall, or more.
record.final_answer:
More — up to 400 requests per minute per key.

Why: `Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key")` at gateway/limits.py:5 passes no backend, so it uses the default `memory` backend. Per the docs, memory counters live inside each process, and "an application with N worker processes lets a key make up to N times the configured rate." deploy/server.conf:2 sets `workers = 4`, and every worker imports the same module-level limiter, so each keeps its own 100/min counter per key → 4 × 100.

Two things that make it worse/looser:

1. No config anywhere in the repo overrides the backend — I grepped for `backend`/`tally` and the only match is that one `Limiter(...)` line, and requirements.txt pins quillon==1.8.2 (the version the docs describe). So memory is definitely in effect.
2. Even after fixing the backend, the docs note windows are fixed and clock-aligned: a key can send 100 at the end of one minute and 100 at the start of the next, i.e. 200 inside a rolling 60s. That's a burst allowance, not a sustained 2x, but it's real.

To actually get 100/min per key overall, point the limiter at the shared backend:

    limiter = Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key",
                      backend="tally", url="tally://host:7070")

That requires a reachable tallyd instance. If you'd rather not run one, the alternative is keeping memory counters and dividing the rate by the worker count (25/minute), which is only accurate while all 4 workers stay up and traffic spreads evenly — I wouldn't rely on it.

I couldn't verify the default-branch behaviour against the installed package (quillon isn't installed in this workspace), so the 400 figure rests on the 1.8 docs matching the pinned 1.8.2.
